items.title: refactor(store): replace TensorSnapshot with burn_pack::Tensor
items.body:
Closes #5378.

`TensorSnapshot` and `burn_pack::Tensor` had converged into two mechanisms for deferred bytes one layer apart. This drops the former, making `burn_pack::Tensor` the single tensor-transport type across the save/load stack.

Container types (`Struct:Linear`) reach adapters as a borrowed `ModuleContext` instead of riding on the tensor, since only adapters read them. `catch_unwind` moves to provider construction in burn-store, so a backend panic stays a typed error without pulling `std` into burn-pack.

Breaking:
- `collect` / `apply` take and return `burn_pack::Tensor`
- `get_snapshot` / `get_all_snapshots` -> `get_tensor` / `get_all_tensors`
- `ModuleAdapter::adapt(tensor, ctx)`
- the `burnpack` feature is gone; burn-pack is now a hard dependency

Two latent bugs fixed along the way: the pickle reader returned f32 zeros regardless of dtype when a storage offset overran, and the PyTorch adapters transposed quantized Linear weights (packed values plus an inline scale tail) into zeros.

Verified: burn-store, burn-pack, burn-core record and pytorch/safetensors integration suites; `cargo doc`; no-std and `thumbv6m-none-eabi` builds.

items.title: Add A-FINE image quality metric
items.body:
## Pull Request Template

### Checklist

- [x] Confirmed that `cargo run-checks` command has been executed.
- [x] Made sure the book is up to date with changes in this PR.

### Related Issues/PRs

Ticks one box on the meta-issue #4312. Original scoping comment + your answers are in that thread.

### Changes

A-FINE is a full-reference image quality metric that runs both the distorted and reference images through CLIP ViT-B/32, then through a naturalness head, a fidelity head, two logistic calibrators, and an adapter that fuses them into one (0, 100) score. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.11221. PyIQA reference: https://github.com/chaofengc/IQA-PyTorch/blob/main/pyiqa/archs/afine_arch.py.

Lives at `crates/burn-train/src/metric/vision/afine/`. CLIP ViT is inlined under the metric, matching what LPIPS, DISTS, and FID did. ~1830 LOC across 8 Rust files plus the burn-book row.

A few things worth flagging:

- The CLIP backbone uses QuickGELU (`x * sigmoid(1.702 * x)`), not erf-based GELU. Substituting silently shifts every MLP activation, so QuickGELU lives as its own private module here, with the coefficient pinned at 1.702 as a labeled constant.
- The attention block is a custom fused-QKV one (`qkv_proj: Linear(d_model, 3 * d_model)` + `chunk(3, -1)` at forward) so the CLIP checkpoint maps to it one-to-one. burn-nn's MultiHeadAttention uses separate Q/K/V Linears, which would force a pre-split at load.
- The naturalness head's MLP uses the erf-based `burn_nn::Gelu`, NOT QuickGELU. PyIQA's reference is explicit on this distinction.
- `c1 = c2 = 1e-10` in the fidelity head's SSIM-like ratios. DISTS uses `1e-6` but A-FINE's CLIP feature magnitudes are unit-scale-ish, so the smaller eps is what the trained checkpoint expects.

Two non-obvious things in the pretrained loader the parity test caught:

The five 0-D scalar params (NR/FR `yita3`, `yita4`, adapter `k`) are stored with `shape=()` in the checkpoint but burn's `Param<Tensor<B, 1>>` expects `(1,)`. PytorchStore silently drops these, leaving them at random init. Loaded manually via `PytorchReader::with_top_level_key(...).get(name)`.

The CLIP checkpoint has both `positional_embedding` (text encoder, shape `[77, 512]`) and `visual.positional_embedding` (shape `[50, 768]`). After my remap renames the visual one to `positional_embedding`, both keys collide and HashMap iteration order picks which wins. Pre-rename of the text encoder's key first dodges the collision.

### Question on weight hosting

The URL points at the PyIQA author's personal HF mirror (`chaofengc/IQA-PyTorch-Weights/resolve/main/afine.pth`). I tried pretty hard to find an org-hosted alternative and couldn't:

- Not on any HF org I checked (PyIQA-related, q-future, the authors' institutions)
- Not in IQA-PyTorch's GitHub releases (50+ other metric weights are there, just not `afine.pth`)
- Not on Zenodo, figshare, ModelScope, OSF, or Kaggle
- Authors' canonical release is Google Drive only, which reqwest can't follow cleanly

I noticed LPIPS, DISTS, and FID currently pull weights from personal-account GitHub raw URLs, so personal hosting isn't unprecedented in burn. But I remember you mentioned org hosting was preferred when we scoped this on the issue, so figured I'd flag rather than assume. Happy to go with whatever you prefer: keep this URL, have tracel-ai mirror `afine.pth`, or another option.

### Testing

Always-on property tests: forward shape, batch processing, finite output on constant inputs, asymmetry from the adapter's exponent term, `image_size` validation, display format.

Two `#[ignore = "downloads pre-trained weights"]` tests, matching the LPIPS/DISTS/FID convention:

- `test_afine_pretrained` loads real weights and checks the score is finite and meaningfully differs from a random-init metric on the same input. Catches silent partial loads where a regex remap is wrong.
- `test_afine_pretrained_parity` matches a captured PyIQA reference scalar on a deterministic `arange/(N-1)` vs `arange/N` input pair to within ~5e-5 absolute. Catches QuickGELU-vs-GELU swaps, fused-QKV transpose-direction bugs, channel-order mistakes, and `c1=c2=1e-10` epsilon drift that the property tests miss.

`cargo run-checks` green: fmt, clippy, audit, typos, doc, full burn-train with `--features vision` (123 passing, 7 ignored).

items.title: Implements: LPIPS matrics for Image quality
items.body:
## Pull Request Template

### Checklist

- [x] Confirmed that `cargo run-checks` command has been executed.
- [x] Made sure the book is up to date with changes in this PR.

### Related Issues/PRs

[Image quality metrics #4312 ](https://github.com/tracel-ai/burn/issues/4312)

### Changes

Follow this references 
[lightning.ai](https://lightning.ai/docs/torchmetrics/stable/image/learned_perceptual_image_patch_similarity.html#), [torch-image-metrics](https://github.com/mdipcit/torch-image-metrics?tab=readme-ov-file#-supported-metrics)

Supported Networks: VGG16, AlexNet, SqueezeNet
  
  Configuration Parameters

  - net - Backbone network type (VGG, Alex, Squeeze)
  - normalize - Whether to normalize input from [0,1] to [-1,1]

  Implementation Details

  The LPIPS metric computes perceptual distance using deep features:

  $$\text{LPIPS}(x, y) = \sum_{l} \frac{1}{H_l W_l} \sum_{h,w}  w_l \odot
  (\hat{f}^l_{x,hw} - \hat{f}^l_{y,hw}) ^2_2$$

  Where:
  - $\hat{f}^l$ = unit-normalized features at layer $l$
  - $w_l$ = learned linear weights (1x1 conv)
  - $H_l, W_l$ = spatial dimensions at layer $l$


Implementation

  1. Extracting multi-scale deep features from backbone network
  2. Computing normalized L2 distance between features
  3. Applying learned linear weights (1x1 conv) and spatial averaging

  Supports loading pretrained weights from PyTorch lpips library via `lpips_key_remaps()`


### Testing

Test Name | Description | Backbone
-- | -- | --
test_lpips_identical_images_zero_loss | Identical images → Loss is exactly 0 | VGG
test_lpips_different_images_positive_loss | Different images → Loss is greater than 0 | VGG
test_lpips_symmetry | Verification that $LPIPS(a, b) = LPIPS(b, a)$ | VGG
test_lpips_forward_mean_reduction | Validates output shape when using mean reduction | VGG
test_lpips_forward_no_reduction | Validates output shape when no reduction is applied | VGG
test_lpips_output_non_negative | Ensures the loss value is always $\ge 0$ | VGG
test_lpips_alex_identical_images_zero_loss | Identical images → Loss is exactly 0 | AlexNet
test_lpips_alex_different_images_positive_loss | Different images → Loss is greater than 0 | AlexNet
test_lpips_squeeze_identical_images_zero_loss | Identical images → Loss is exactly 0 | SqueezeNet
test_lpips_squeeze_different_images_positive_loss | Different images → Loss is greater than 0 | SqueezeNet
display_vgg | Validates the display string format | VGG
display_alex | Validates the display string format | AlexNet
display_squeeze | Validates the display string format | SqueezeNet


### Example

**I make the examples for compareing pytorch. If Don't need it I remove this examples** 

File / Directory | Description
-- | --
src/main.rs | Loads PyTorch weights and compares Burn vs. PyTorch outputs.
compare.py | Generates weights and runs the PyTorch side of the comparison.
img/*.raw | Test images stored in 64x64 f32 raw format.
weights/*.pt | Pretrained PyTorch weights (VGG, AlexNet, SqueezeNet).


Network | Test Case | Burn Value | PyTorch Value | Match
-- | -- | -- | -- | --
VGG | zeros vs ones | 0.453837 | 0.453837 | ✓
VGG | horizontal vs vertical | 0.667304 | 0.667304 | ✓
VGG | horizontal vs diagonal | 0.350121 | 0.350121 | ✓
AlexNet | zeros vs ones | 0.813955 | 0.813955 | ✓
AlexNet | horizontal vs vertical | 0.674660 | 0.674660 | ✓

items.title: Add contiguous reindexing for non-contiguous layer indices
items.body:
Problem

When PyTorch models use `nn.Sequential` with mixed layer types (e.g., Conv2d + ReLU), the state_dict keys have non-contiguous indices because only layers with parameters are saved:

```python
self.fc = nn.Sequential(
  nn.Conv2d(...),  # fc.0.weight, fc.0.bias
  nn.ReLU(),       # No parameters (index 1 skipped)
  nn.Conv2d(...),  # fc.2.weight, fc.2.bias
  nn.ReLU(),       # No parameters (index 3 skipped)
  nn.Conv2d(...),  # fc.4.weight, fc.4.bias
)
```

Burn models expect contiguous indices (fc.0, fc.1, fc.2), causing loading failures without manual remapping.

Solution

Added a reindex_contiguous() function that automatically remaps non-contiguous indices:
```
- fc.0.weight → fc.0.weight
- fc.2.weight → fc.1.weight
- fc.4.weight → fc.2.weight
```
 
API

```rust
// PytorchStore: contiguous_reindex is ON by default
let mut store = PytorchStore::from_file("model.pth");

// Disable if needed
let mut store = PytorchStore::from_file("model.pth")
    .contiguous_reindex(false);

// SafetensorsStore: contiguous_reindex is OFF by default
let mut store = SafetensorsStore::from_file("model.safetensors")
    .contiguous_reindex(true);  // Enable for PyTorch-exported safetensors
```

### Checklist

- [x] Confirmed that `cargo run-checks` command has been executed.
- [x] Made sure the book is up to date with changes in this PR.

### Related Issues/PRs

Closes #4149

### Changes
- Add automatic contiguous reindexing for `PytorchStore` and `SafetensorsStore` to handle PyTorch models with non-contiguous layer indices
- Enable reindexing by default for `PytorchStore` (common use case), disable by default for `SafetensorsStore`
- Add `contiguous_reindex(bool)` builder method to both stores


### Testing
- Unit tests for reindex_contiguous() function (6 tests)
- Integration tests for PytorchStore with non-contiguous indices
- Tests verifying behavior with reindexing enabled vs disabled
- All burn-store tests passing

items.title: Add configurable activation and layer_norm_eps to transformer layers
items.body:
## Summary

- Add `gelu_approximate` free function to `burn-tensor::activation` (tanh-based GELU matching PyTorch `gelu(approximate="tanh")`) with precomputed `sqrt(2/pi)` constant
- Add `approximate` field to `Gelu` module (`Gelu::new()` for exact, `Gelu::new_approximate()` for tanh approximation)
- Replace hardcoded `Gelu` in `PositionWiseFeedForward` with configurable `activation: ActivationConfig` (default: `Gelu`)
- Add `activation` and `layer_norm_eps` config fields to both `TransformerEncoderConfig` and `TransformerDecoderConfig`
- Fix decoder not passing `initializer` to `PositionWiseFeedForwardConfig`

## Motivation

Models like ALBERT, GPT-2, and others use different FFN activations (approximate GELU, ReLU, SwiGLU). Previously `PositionWiseFeedForward` hardcoded `Gelu`, forcing downstream models to reimplement the entire feed-forward layer. Now any `ActivationConfig` variant can be used.

Similarly, `layer_norm_eps` was hardcoded to the `LayerNormConfig` default (1e-5), but models like ALBERT specify different values in their configs.

## Test plan

- [x] `Gelu::new_approximate()` forward test with values verified against PyTorch `torch.nn.functional.gelu(x, approximate="tanh")`
- [x] `ActivationConfig::GeluApproximate` wrapper test
- [x] All existing burn-nn tests pass (252 tests)
- [x] Display test updated for new Gelu struct format
- [x] albert-burn pretrained integration tests pass with correct logits

items.title: Add `burn-store` crate for model storage with safetensors support
items.body:
## Pull Request Overview

This PR introduces `burn-store`, a new crate providing advanced model storage and serialization capabilities for
Burn. It implements comprehensive safetensors support with cross-framework interoperability, enabling seamless PyTorch <--> Burn model conversion, efficient large model handling through lazy loading, and flexible tensor filtering/remapping
capabilities.

### Checklist

- [x] Confirmed that `cargo run-checks` command has been executed.
- [x] Made sure the book is up to date with changes in this PR. (Should we add a book section?)

### Related Issues/PRs

* Fixes https://github.com/tracel-ai/burn/issues/3260
* Fixes https://github.com/tracel-ai/burn/issues/3598

### Changes

#### New `burn-store` Crate
- **Core Infrastructure**: New crate with `ModuleSnapshot` trait and `TensorSnapshot` system for efficient tensor
management
- **SafeTensors Integration**: Full support for the industry-standard SafeTensors format with zero-copy loading via memory mapping
- **Lazy Evaluation**: Tensor transformations are composed as closures and only materialized when needed, reducing memory usage
- **No-std Support**: Core functionality available in embedded and WASM environments

#### Cross-Framework Interoperability
- **Framework Adapters**: `PyTorchToBurnAdapter` and `BurnToPyTorchAdapter` for automatic tensor transformations
  - Automatic weight transposition for Linear/Conv layers
  - Parameter renaming (gamma→weight, beta→bias for normalization layers)
  - Lazy transformation chaining without intermediate materialization
- **Tensor Remapping**: Regex-based tensor name transformations via `KeyRemapper`
- **Custom Adapters**: Extensible `ModuleAdapter` trait for framework-specific transformations

#### Advanced Filtering and Configuration
- **Builder Pattern API**: Fluent interface for configuration
  - `with_regex()`, `with_full_path()`, `with_predicate()` for filtering
  - `with_key_pattern()` for inline remapping
  - `with_from_adapter()`, `with_to_adapter()` for framework conversions
- **Partial Loading**: Continue loading even when tensors are missing (`allow_partial`)
- **Custom Metadata**: Attach version info and other metadata to saved models
- **Validation Control**: Optional tensor validation during loading

#### Performance Optimizations
- **Memory-Mapped Files**: Automatic use of mmap for efficient large file access
- **Lazy Tensor Materialization**: Tensors only loaded when accessed via `Rc<dyn Fn() -> TensorData>`
- **Streaming Saves**: Direct-to-disk writing without full memory buffering
- **Selective Loading**: Filter tensors before materialization to reduce memory usage

### Testing

- Comprehensive test suite with 73+ tests covering:
  - SafeTensors file I/O and memory operations
  - PyTorch adapter transformations (weight transposition, parameter renaming)
  - Filtering with regex, exact paths, and predicates
  - Tensor remapping and key transformations
  - Lazy evaluation and memory efficiency
  - Error handling and edge cases
  - No-std compatibility

### Examples

```rust
// Load PyTorch model with automatic conversions
let mut store = SafetensorsStore::from_file("pytorch_model.safetensors")
    .with_from_adapter(PyTorchToBurnAdapter)     // Auto-transpose weights
    .with_regex(r"^transformer\..*")             // Only load transformer
    .with_key_pattern(r"\.attn\.", ".attention.") // Rename layers
    .allow_partial(true);                        // Skip unknown tensors

model.apply_from(&mut store)?;
```


Benchmarks are down below: https://github.com/tracel-ai/burn/pull/3666#issuecomment-3277610680

items.title: Optimize argument handling and improve ONNX graph building
items.body:
## Pull Request Template

### Checklist

- [x] Confirmed that `run-checks all` script has been executed.
- [ ] Made sure the book is up to date with changes in this PR.

### Related Issues/PRs

#1840
 
### Changes
This was the alternative design I was talking about the other day. It's definitely a different set of compromises compared to #1795. 


1. got rid of `graph_io`, and move renaming to the end, which mostly works
2. I altered how arguments are added to the map, so that it only runs on inputs (which mostly works). 
3. Args are cloned into nodes, so functions that examine inputs or alter outputs don't need a second struct.

#### Problems
- in order to check if inputs are passed, since input names are altered at the beginning, we need to double map them (new_name->old->name->entry). This is both marginally better if a graph has 50+ inputs, and needed to check if the input is also an initializer(both are the case for web inference example).
- In order for unsqueeze to remap to a reshape(if the shape of the lhs is unknown or symbolic), it needs to check if the rhs is a graph output, which right now feels a little bolted on because nothing else needs access to that.

### Testing

testing with existing onnx test, and the minst classification web example. passes the test, both work as expected. 

I figured out why the example was failing before. All but the first input are also initializers.

items.body: ## Pull Request Template ### Checklist - [x] Confirmed that `run-checks all` script has been executed. - [x] Made sure the book is up to date with changes in this PR. ### Related Issues/PRs None, just adding `unsqueeze_dims` to get us closer to full `ONNX` support ### Changes adds a new function `unsqueeze_dims` to `burn-tensor/src/tensor/api/base`, which takes a slice of isizes as the second argument (to make it compatible with the [onnx unsqeeze op](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/main/docs/Operators.md#Unsqueeze). For burn import, if the rhs of the op node is constant, the output shape is calculated, if it isn't and the output shape has an explicit value already, the op is replaced with a reshape. it might be desireable to just remap to reshape in every case if the output shape is explicit. and/or to truncate multiple unsqueezes to a single unsqueeze. as we were discussing on the discord a while ago, this implementation doesn't yet support the third case: where the dimensions of the output are symbolic (determined by the outputs of previous steps at runtime), but I'm not sure if supporting that would be possible in burn right now for any op. ### Testing There was a discrepancy between the unsqueeze function for torch and ONNX. Torch only supported as single axis argument, ONNX supported multiple, so I wrote some code to generate the Onnx model directly through Onnx helper and runtime. We might want to move it into it's own directory to use as a python module if we want to use it for other operations. right now the onnx model takes a second input argument that is not present in the burn forward function, but I needed the second op to test remapping to a reshape node. items.title: Add support for loading PyTorch `.pt` (weights/states) files directly to model's record
items.body:
This PR introduces a new feature for loading PyTorch `.pt` files using Recorder.

**Key Highlights:**

1. **Loading `.pt` Files:**
   ```rust
   let record = PyTorchFileRecorder::<FullPrecisionSettings>::default()
       .load("mypytorchweights.pt".into())
       .expect("Failed to decode state");

   let model = MyModel::<B>::new_with(record);
   ```

2. **Remapping Levels/Keys:**
   Aligning the source model's levels/keys with the target model (detailed explanation in the book):
   ```rust
   let load_args = LoadArgs::new("mypytorchweights.pt".into())
       .with_key_remap("conv\\.(.*)", "$1"); // Removes "conv" prefix, e.g., "conv.conv1" -> "conv1"

   let record = PyTorchFileRecorder::<FullPrecisionSettings>::default()
       .load(load_args)
       .expect("Failed to decode state");

   let model = MyModel::<Backend>::new_with(record);
   ```

3. **Compatibility with Burn's Modules:**
   The loader uses special adapters to match Burn's NN module structure. For example, Linear's weight is stored as `[in, out]` in Burn, whereas PyTorch stores it as `[out, in]`. This implementation facilitates ongoing development in Burn without needing to conform to PyTorch's format.

4. **Dynamic Loading and Deployment:**
   Dynamic loading from PyTorch files is not necessary for deployments. The `pytorch-import` example shows how to convert a `pt` file to Burn's format during build time, thus removing the need to link to the Pickle library (candle-core in our case).

**Current Limitations:**

1. Candle's pickle library does not currently function on Windows due to this bug: [Candle Issue #1454](https://github.com/huggingface/candle/issues/1454). Burn issue ticket: https://github.com/tracel-ai/burn/issues/1178
2. Candle's pickle does not currently unpack boolean tensors. Burn issue ticket: https://github.com/tracel-ai/burn/issues/1179.

## Pull Request Template

### Checklist

- [x] Confirmed execution of the `run-checks all` script.
- [ ] Ensuring the book is updated with the changes in this PR. (TODO: I am still working on this)

### Changes

1. Enhanced `burn-import` to add the PyTorch feature with `PyTorchFileRecorder`.
2. Refactored record implementation for `[T;N]` to avoid conversion into `Vec[T]` in `primitive.rs`. Instead, implemented serde for the `[T;N]` type. This is necessary to set default values for `[T;N]`, e.g., `kernel_size` in `conv2d`. It's impractical to set a default value for `Vec[T]` and convert to `[T;N]` because the default for a `Vec` is an empty vector, which cannot be converted to `[T;N]`.
3. Added a `record-serde` feature in `burn-core` that can take a `NestedValue` object and deserialize it into a `RecordItem`. This is used by `PyTorchFileRecorder` in `burn-import` and can also be utilized by other formats, e.g., Safetensor.

### Testing

Added a `pytorch-tests` sub-crate in `burn-import` that thoroughly tests all NN models and scenarios using actual PyTorch `pt` files.
